title: Capacitor charging and discharging; RC circuits by differential equation
qualification: AP Physics C: Electricity and Magnetism
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics C: Electricity and Magnetism (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EL10-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; EL10-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; EL10-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; NEW-RC-calc-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EL10-1#N.8, NEW-RC-calc-1#N.2, NEW-RC-calc-1#N.5, NEW-RC-calc-1#N.8, NEW-RC-calc-1#N.9.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Current
items.clue: Equal to the gradient of a Q–t graph.

items.label: Charge
items.clue: Equal to the area under an I–t graph.

items.label: Exponential decay
items.clue: Fall in which the rate of loss is proportional to the amount left.

items.label: Loop rule
items.clue: Statement used to write ε – IR – q/C = 0 for a series battery, resistor and capacitor.

questions.stem: An uncharged capacitor is charged through a 3.0 kΩ resistor by an ideal battery of emf 9.0 V, all connected in series. What is the current in the resistor at the instant when the potential difference across the capacitor is 6.0 V?

An uncharged capacitor of capacitance C is connected in series with a resistor of resistance R, a switch and an ideal battery of emf ε, and the switch is closed at t = 0. Let q be the charge on the capacitor. At the instant when q = Cε/4, what is dq/dt?

An uncharged capacitor of capacitance C, a resistor of resistance R and an ideal battery of emf ε are connected in series, and the circuit is completed at t = 0. By solving the loop-rule equation ε = (dq/dt)R + q/C, find the time t at which the current in the resistor is half its initial value.
An uncharged 50 μF capacitor is connected in series with a 20 kΩ resistor, an open switch and an ideal 9.0 V battery. The switch is closed at t = 0. What is the current in the resistor at t = 2.0 s?

A capacitor of capacitance C is charged, disconnected from the battery and then, at t = 0, connected across a resistor of resistance R. At what time t is the energy stored in the capacitor half of its value at t = 0?
